models.deep.modules.efficient_graph_convolution module¶

Optimized Graph Convolution implementation with multiple aggregators.

class models.deep.modules.efficient_graph_convolution.EfficientGraphConvolution(in_channels: int, out_channels: int, aggrs: Iterable[str] = ('symnorm',), num_heads: int = 8, num_bases: int = 4, cached: bool = False, add_self_loops: bool = True, bias: bool = True, sigmoid: bool = False, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: MessagePassing

Efficient Graph Convolution (EGC) with multiple aggregators.

This layer computes node updates using a linear combination of different neighborhood aggregations (mean, max, sum, var, std, symnorm) and self-features. Supports multi-head weights and basis functions for efficiency.

models.deep.modules.gated_graph_convolution module¶

Gated Graph Convolution (GatedGCN) with explicit edge updates.

class models.deep.modules.gated_graph_convolution.GatedGraphConvolution(hidden_dim: int, aggregation: str = 'sum', norm: str = 'batch', activation: str = 'relu', learn_affine: bool = True, gated: bool = True, bias: bool = True)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Implements the Gated Graph ConvNet layer:

h_i = ReLU ( U*h_i + Aggr.( sigma_ij, V*h_j) ), sigma_ij = sigmoid( A*h_i + B*h_j + C*e_ij ), e_ij = ReLU ( A*h_i + B*h_j + C*e_ij ), where Aggr. is an aggregation function: sum/mean/max.

References

    1. Bresson and T. Laurent. An experimental study of neural networks for variable graphs. In International Conference on Learning Representations, 2018.

      1. Dwivedi, C. K. Joshi, T. Laurent, Y. Bengio, and X. Bresson. Benchmarking graph neural networks. arXiv preprint arXiv:2003.00982, 2020.

  • Vh – Neighborhood features (B x V x V x H)

Returns:

Aggregated neighborhood features (B x V x H)

parallel_scan_dummy(u, delta, A, B, C)[source]¶

A simplified sequential implementation of the SSM equation: h_t = A_t * h_{t-1} + B_t * x_t y_t = C_t * h_t

Note: Production Mamba uses a hardware-aware parallel scan here.

models.deep.modules.multi_head_attention module¶

Multi-Head Attention mechanism for transformer architectures.

class models.deep.modules.multi_head_attention.MultiHeadAttention(n_heads: int, input_dim: int, embed_dim: int | None = None, val_dim: int | None = None, key_dim: int | None = None)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Multi-Head Attention mechanism.

Allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. Implements scaled dot-product attention.

forward(q, h=None, mask=None)[source]¶

Computes the multi-head attention.

Parameters:

  • q – Queries tensor of shape (batch_size, n_query, input_dim).

  • h – Key/Value keys tensor of shape (batch_size, graph_size, input_dim). If None, defaults to q (self-attention).

  • mask – Attention mask of shape (batch_size, n_query, graph_size). Should contain 1 (or > -inf) if attention is not possible, usually used as additive mask.

Returns:

Context vectors (aggregated values) of shape (batch_size, n_query, embed_dim). attn: Attention weights (batch_size, n_heads, n_query, graph_size).

Return type:

context

init_parameters()[source]¶

Initializes the parameters of the attention layers using Xavier uniform initialization.
